ties.applies_to: any office, as canvassed by the board of state canvassers (statewide offices, offices of the multi-county districts, presidential electors)
ties.steps: if 2 or more individuals have an equal and the highest number of votes for an office, as canvassed by the board of state canvassers, the tie is resolved under section 852: the board of canvassers, after notice to each of the candidates of a time and place, determines the successful candidate by lot and declares and certifies it; the lot does not preclude a defeated candidate's right to a recount
ties.who: the board of canvassers (the board of state canvassers)

sources.quote: If 2 or more individuals have an equal and the highest number of votes for any office, as canvassed by the board of state canvassers, the tie must be resolved and the winner certified as provided under section 852.
the board of canvassers, after notice to each of such candidates of a time and place therefor, shall determine the successful candidate by lot and shall declare and certify the same accordingly.

ties.note: MCL 168.846 and 168.852 (852 applies where no other provision of the act determines the tie; none was found for these offices). Which offices the board of state canvassers canvasses is set in MCL 168.841 and following, not read; the kinds list is [inferred] from the statewide and multi-county offices it names in 168.879. For Governor, no tie provision was found in Article V of the Constitution of 1963 (searched), so 852 applies as the act's general rule [inferred]. Each house of the legislature is the judge of its members' elections under Art. IV, sec. 16 of the Constitution (MCL 168.879(4) refers to it; its text was not read), so a legislative seat may still be decided there.

ties.applies_to: any election canvassed by the board of county canvassers (county, township, city, school district and other local offices; legislative and congressional districts wholly within one county)
ties.steps: the board of canvassers for the county appoints a day for the tied persons to appear before the county clerk, who prepares slips of paper (one marked 'elected' for each office to be filled, the rest 'not elected'), and each person draws one; whoever draws 'elected' is elected and the county clerk gives a certificate of election; if the office of county clerk is in question the drawing is before the sheriff; the lot does not preclude a defeated candidate's right to a recount
ties.who: the county clerk (the sheriff if the county clerk's office is in question), on the appointment of the board of county canvassers

sources.quote: If it shall appear on the canvass of the votes polled at any election canvassed by the board of county canvassers that 2 or more persons have received an equal number of votes for the same office, and that a failure to elect to any office is caused thereby, the election to the office shall be determined in the following manner
for the purpose of determining by lot among such persons the right to the office

ties.note: MCL 168.851. The section reads "any election canvassed by the board of county canvassers"; which offices that is (MCL 168.841 and following; MCL 168.879(1)(a) says the state representative, state senator and Representative in Congress of a district wholly within one county are among them) is a reading, not the text of a list. State general law only; city and township charters were not read.

ties.applies_to: a primary election, for any office
ties.steps: the returns of a primary are canvassed and the results declared in the same manner, within the same time and by the same officers as for general elections; a tie for the one nomination is decided by lot by the board of canvassers (852; or before the county clerk under 851 for a county canvass)
ties.who: the board of canvassers for the office

sources.quote: The returns of a primary election must be canvassed and the results declared in the same manner and within the same time after the primary election and by the same officers as provided for general elections.

In case it shall appear that 2 or more persons have an equal number of votes for the same office for which but 1 person is to be nominated or elected and the same shall be the highest number of votes cast therefor, and no other provision is made in this act for determination of such tie, the board of canvassers

ties.note: MCL 168.581(1) and 168.852, which says "nominated or elected". A tie for second place or for more than one nomination in a multi-seat primary was not separately treated by any section read.

threshold.percent_of: the total number of votes cast in that statewide election
threshold.conditions: does not apply to partisan offices to which more than 1 individual is to be elected; not conducted if the losing candidate (or losing ballot question committee) files a written waiver with the secretary of state within 48 hours after certification
threshold.in_words: a recount of all precincts is conducted automatically when a statewide primary or election is certified as decided by a vote differential of 0.1% or less of the votes cast, unless the loser files a waiver within 48 hours

recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read (the petition deposits of 168.881 apply to petitions under 168.879 and 168.880, not to a recount required by 168.880a)

sources.quote: a recount of all precincts in this state must be conducted at any time a statewide primary or election is certified by the board of state canvassers as having been determined by a vote differential of 0.1% or less of the total number of votes cast in that statewide election.

the recount required under this section must not be conducted if, within 48 hours after the election is certified, the losing candidate files a written statement with the secretary of state requesting that the recount required under this section not be conducted.

recounts.note: MCL 168.880a(1) and (6), as amended by 2024 PA 74 (effective April 2, 2025). "Statewide election" covers the offices on the statewide ballot (Governor, U.S. Senator and the like) and statewide ballot questions [inferred from subsection (5), which provides for a ballot question].

recounts.election: state senate election, other than a primary

threshold.conditions: all precincts of the state senate district; general election only; waivable by the losing candidate within 48 hours after certification
threshold.in_words: a recount of the whole state senate district is automatic at a vote differential of 75 votes or less in a general election

recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read

sources.quote: a recount of all precincts in a state senate district must be conducted at any time a state senate election, other than a state senate primary election, is certified by the board of state canvassers or a board of county canvassers as having been determined by a vote differential of 75 votes or less.

recounts.election: state representative election, other than a primary

threshold.conditions: all precincts of the state representative district; general election only; waivable by the losing candidate within 48 hours after certification
threshold.in_words: a recount of the whole state representative district is automatic at a vote differential of 25 votes or less in a general election

recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read

sources.quote: a recount of all precincts in a state representative district must be conducted at any time a state representative election, other than a state representative primary election, is certified by the board of state canvassers or a board of county canvassers as having been determined by a vote differential of 25 votes or less.

threshold.conditions: the petitioner must be a candidate for the office who can allege a good-faith belief that, but for error in the canvass or returns, the candidate would have had a reasonable chance of winning; the number of votes requested to be recounted must be greater than the difference between the petitioner and the winning candidate; filed within 48 hours after the county canvass is certified (with the secretary of state by 5 p.m. of the second day after the state canvass is certified)
threshold.in_words: any candidate with a good-faith belief of a reasonable chance of winning may petition for a recount of one or more precincts, whatever the margin; the party chairperson may petition for a state senate race decided by 500 votes or less or a state representative race decided by 200 votes or less

who_may_request: a candidate for the office, by petition filed with the county canvassers' clerk (offices canvassed by the county) or with the secretary of state (offices canvassed by the board of state canvassers, and Representative in Congress, state representative or state senator for a district wholly within one county)
the chairperson of a state political party on behalf of a candidate in a state senate race decided by 500 votes or less or a state representative race decided by 200 votes or less
recounts.cost_bearer: the petitioner, by a deposit of $50.00 per precinct, rising to $250 and $500 per precinct with the margin (see the next rule), refunded if the recount establishes sufficient error to change the result

sources.quote: A candidate is aggrieved if the candidate is able to allege a good-faith belief that, but for error in the canvass or returns of the votes, the candidate would have had a reasonable chance of winning the election.

If a state senatorial race is determined by a vote differential of 500 votes or less or a state representative race is determined by a vote differential of 200 votes or less, the chairperson of a state political party may petition for a recount of the votes on behalf of a candidate in that race in the manner prescribed in subsection (1).

recounts.note: MCL 168.862, 168.866(3), 168.879(1) and (2). There is no margin limit in the sections read, only the good-faith belief and the rule that the votes recounted must exceed the difference. A recount under this chapter is an administrative process limited to counting the votes (168.861(2)).

recounts.election: any primary or election, with a larger deposit beyond the margin

threshold.percent_of: the total number of votes cast in the race
threshold.conditions: one candidate to be elected: deposit $50 per precinct up to a difference of the greater of 50 votes or 0.5% of the votes cast; $250 per precinct beyond that; $500 per precinct beyond the greater of 75 votes or 5.0%; state canvass tiers for statewide offices: $250 over 2,000 votes and $500 over 4,000 votes (statewide primaries: $250 over 700 and $500 over 1,400); state senate: $250 over 75 votes and $500 over 150; state representative: $250 over 25 votes and $500 over 50
threshold.in_words: a petitioner pays $50 per precinct when the margin is small and more per precinct as the margin grows, and the deposit is refunded if the recount changes the result

who_may_request: the petitioning candidate, as in the rule above
recounts.cost_bearer: the petitioner, by a deposit per precinct; refunded when the recount establishes sufficient error to change the result; otherwise paid to the county treasurers

sources.quote: if 1 candidate is to be elected to the office and the official canvass of votes shows that the number of votes separating the winning candidate and the petitioner is more than 50 votes or 0.5% of the total number of votes cast in the race, whichever is greater, the petitioner shall deposit with the clerk the sum of $250.00 for each precinct referred to in the petitioner's recount petition.

If, by reason of the recount, the petitioner establishes sufficient error to change the result of the election, the clerk of the board of county canvassers shall refund the money deposited to the petitioner.

recounts.note: MCL 168.867 (petitions to the county canvassers) and 168.881 (petitions to the board of state canvassers, with the statewide, state senate and state representative tiers); the amounts are to be adjusted for inflation from January 1, 2027 (168.867(8), 168.881(16)).

recounts.election: any election with a ballot question

threshold.conditions: a ballot question committee that participated in the election (or, if none did, any elector who voted) that believes that, but for error, the outcome would have been the opposite; the number of votes requested to be recounted must be greater than the difference between the yes and no votes; a statewide question: filed with the secretary of state by 5 p.m. of the second day after the board of state canvassers certifies the results
threshold.in_words: a ballot question committee (or an elector) may petition for a recount whatever the margin, in good faith and on a belief that the outcome would have been the opposite but for error; a deposit of $50 per precinct, more beyond 0.5% or 75 votes

who_may_request: a ballot question committee that participated in the election, or any elector who voted if none did
recounts.cost_bearer: the petitioner, by a deposit per precinct, refunded if the recount changes the result

sources.quote: that ballot question committee believes that, but for error, the outcome of the ballot question would have been the opposite result, that ballot question committee may file a recount petition of the votes cast on that ballot question in any precinct.

unread.what: MCL 168.841 and following (which board canvasses which office), MCL 168.894 (who bears the expense of a recount by county boards), the Michigan Constitution Art. IV sec. 16 text, and city, township and school district charters; any tie rule for a ballot question or for presidential electors outside the sections read

notes: Michigan settles every tie in the sections read by lot by the board of canvassers (MCL 168.846, 168.851, 168.852); no section was found for a tie in a ballot question.

Michigan's automatic recounts changed on April 2, 2025 (2024 PA 74): statewide 0.1%, state senate 75 votes, state representative 25 votes; the senate and house triggers exclude primaries; each is waivable by the loser within 48 hours.
